ANDROTELO.Titre complet: Essai Bayésien de phase I/II évaluant l’efficacité et la tolérance du danazol chez les patients ayant une atteinte hématologique ou pulmonaire sévère liée à une téloméropathie
ANDROTELO.Investigateur coordonnateur: Dr Flore Sicre de Fontbrune, Hématologie greffe, Hôpital Saint-Louis, Paris
ANDROTELO.Justification scientifique: Les mutations constitutionnelles des gènes impliqués dans la réparation et la maintenance des télomères sont responsables des « téloméropathies » (« Dyskératose Congénitale »). L’attrition des télomères favorise la senescence cellulaire et l’instabilité génétique. La pénétrance et la sévérité des atteintes d’organes (pulmonaires, hématologiques, hépatiques, et neurologiques) est variable, dépendant du gène impliqué, de la génération concernée (phénomène d’anticipation) et aussi de facteurs environnementaux. En cas d’insuffisance médullaire, le seul traitement hématologique curatif est l’allogreffe de cellules souches hématopoïétiques, souvent limitée par une atteinte pulmonaire et/ou hépatique ou l’absence de donneur HLA compatible. Le phénotype pulmonaire est le plus souvent celui d‘une fibrose pulmonaire idiopathique. Dans les formes sévères, une transplantation pulmonaire est proposée en l’absence de contre-indication. Les traitements anti-fibrosants évalués sont peu efficaces ou non évalués. La décroissance observée de la capacité vitale de ces patients est de 300 ml/an, anormalement élevée par rapport aux formes idiopathiques. L’évolution sans greffe est dans les deux situations rapidement défavorable ; le pronostic post greffe pulmonaire ou de moelle est aussi moins bon que celui de greffes similaires hors téloméropathie. Le danazol est utilisé depuis plus de 4 décennies dans les insuffisances médullaires acquises et constitutionnelles en l’absence d’alternative thérapeutique. Dans les téloméropathies, des données rétrospectives sur de petites cohortes font état d’un taux de réponse hématologique de l’ordre de 60 à 70%. Une étude prospective aux Etats Unis a montré récemment une réponse hématologique à 1 an dans 78% des cas (10 des 12 patients évaluables) avec stabilisation de la capacité vitale. Les données rétrospectives (non publiées) sur les patients traités en France sont en faveur d’effets indésirables et d’interruptions de traitement beaucoup plus fréquents et d’une efficacité moindre.
ANDROTELO.Objectif et critère d’évaluation princip: Objectif : Evaluer le bénéfice à 12 mois du danazol sur la réponse clinique. Critère d’évaluation : Pour les patients présentant une insuffisance médullaire, la réponse hématologique à 12 mois en fonction de la ou des lignées atteintes : • augmentation de 1,5 point de l’hémoglobine (g/dL) sans transfusion depuis 2 mois • et/ou augmentation de 20 G/L du compte plaquettaire sans transfusion depuis 2 mois • et/ou augmentation de 0,5 G/L du compte de polynucléaires neutrophiles. Pour les patients présentant une fibrose pulmonaire, une diminution de moins de 5% de la capacité vitale forcée à 12 mois
ANDROTELO.Objectifs et critères d’évaluation secon: Objectifs Evaluer : • la tolérance hépatique et extra hépatique du danazol dans cette indication, • la corrélation entre la réponse clinique et l’évolution de la longueur des télomères, • l’apparition d’anomalies cytologiques et cytogénétiques médullaires sous traitement, • l’apparition d’anomalies parenchymateuses pulmonaires sous traitement, • la qualité de vie des patients, • la survie des patients. Critères d’évaluation Pour tous les patients : • Tolérance hépatique (biologique à 1, 2, 3, 6, 9 et 12 mois, imagerie par échographie à 6 mois et IRM à 12 mois), • Tolérance systémique : endocrinologique (virilisation, poids, glycémie, LDL, HDL cholestérol et triglycérides) à 3, 6, 9, 12 mois, osseuse (évènements osseux et modification de l’ostéo-densitométrie) à 12 mois, musculaire (crampes et enzymes musculaires) à 3, 6, 9 et 12 mois, augmentation des PSA à 3, 6 et 12 mois pour les hommes, • Evolution des anomalies parenchymateuses pulmonaires au scanner à 6 et 12 mois, • Evolution de la longueur des télomères par Flow Fish à 12 mois, • Apparition d‘anomalies cytologiques et cytogénétiques à 12 mois (myélogramme avec caryotype à M12), • Qualité de vie (EORTC QLQ-C30, v3.0) à 3, 6 et 12 mois, • Survie à 3, 6, 9 et 12 mois. Pour les patients ayant une insuffisance médullaire • Réponse hématologique à 3, 6 et 9 mois, • Réponse hématologique complète à 3, 6, 9 et 12 mois (Hb > 10 g/dL, PNN > 1 G/L et plaquettes > 100 G/L) sans transfusion depuis 2 mois, • Indépendance transfusionnelle à 3, 6, 9 et 12 mois, • Evolution de la capacité vitale forcée et de la DLCO à 6 et 12 mois, • Evolution des anomalies parenchymateuses pulmonaires au scanner à 12 mois. Pour les patients ayant une fibrose pulmonaire : • Variation de l’hémogramme sous traitement à 3, 6 et 12 mois, • Evolution de la capacité vitale forcée à 3, 6, 9 mois, • Evolution de la DLCO à 3, 6, 9 et 12 mois, • Evolution des anomalies parenchymateuses pulmonaires au scanner à 6 et 12 mois.
ANDROTELO.Schéma expérimental: Essai thérapeutique de phase 1/2 non contrôlé, en ouvert, bayésien, et stratifié sur la pathologie
ANDROTELO.Population concernée: Patients âgés de plus de 15 ans présentant des atteintes hématologiques ou pulmonaires de téloméropathies.
ANDROTELO.Critères d’inclusion: Patient(e)s: - ayant une téloméropathie définie par l’existence d’une mutation délétère constitutionnelle d’un gène impliqué dans la maintenance des télomères (TERT, TERC, DKC1, TINF2, RTEL1, PARN, ACD, NHP2, NOP10, NAF1, WRAP53, CTC1, ERCC6L2, USB1, POT1, DNAJC21 ou d’un gène nouvellement identifié comme responsable d’une téloméropathie), - âgés de 15 ans ou plus, - ayant une atteinte hématologique sévère (plaquettes < 30 G/L ou PNN < 0,5 G/L et/ou hémoglobine < 9 g/dL et/ou avoir besoin de transfusions) et/ou une fibrose pulmonaire avec une atteinte parenchymateuse supérieure à 10% au scanner. - étant en mesure de donner son consentement éclairé pour les patients de 18 ans et plus, - étant en mesure de donner son consentement et avoir le consentement du ou des titulaire(s) de l’autorité parentale pour les enfants de plus de 15 ans, - Contraception efficace pour les femmes en âge de procréer pendant toute la recherche - étant bénéficiaire d’un régime de sécurité sociale.
ANDROTELO.Critères de non inclusion: Patient(e)s : - ayant une infection par le VIH ou infection active par l’hépatite B ou l’hépatite C, - ayant une atteinte hépatique sévère : transaminases ASAT et/ou ALAT > 5N, ou une bilirubinémie conjuguée > 30 μmol/L, un TP <50% (sauf carence en vitamine K), - ayant une pathologie tumorale active ou traitée depuis moins de 5 ans à l’exception d‘un carcinome basocellulaire ou d’un carcinome in situ du col utérin, - ayant un antécédent de greffe d’organe ou de cellules souches hématopoïétiques ou ayant une indication de greffe de cellules souches hématopoïétiques ou de greffe d’organe dans les 6 mois suivant l’inclusion, - ayant une contre-indication absolue au traitement par danazol : thrombose évolutive ou antécédent de maladie thrombo-embolique, porphyrie, insuffisance rénale ou cardiaque sévère (stade III ou IV de la NYHA), tumeur androgéno-dépendante, nodules mammaires non caractérisés, hémorragie génitale pathologique d’étiologie indéterminée, - ayant déjà reçu du danazol pour le traitement de la téloméropathie, - ayant reçu un autre androgène dans un délai de moins de 6 mois, - recevant un autre traitement expérimental, - recevant un autre traitement hormonal, - recevant un traitement par Simvastatine, par un analogue de la thrombopoïétine (eltrombopag, romiplostine, ou autre), ciclosporine, sérum anti- lymphocytaire et autre traitement immunosuppresseur, GCSF, érythropoïétine, pirfenidone (à l’exception des patients recevant ce traitement à une dose stable depuis plus de 3 mois et pendant la durée du traitement), nintedanib (à l’exception des patients recevant ce traitement à une dose stable depuis plus de 3 mois et pendant la durée du traitement), autre inhibiteur de tyrosine kinase, corticothérapie (autorisée si prescrite depuis plus de 3 mois à dose stable ou décroissante), - ayant un projet de grossesse et ne pas s’engager à avoir une contraception efficace pendant la prise du traitement, - allaitante, - sous tutelle ou curatelle.
ANDROTELO.Traitement(s) à l’essai: DANAZOL 200 mg sous forme de gélules 800 mg/j par voie orale, en 2 prises Durée du traitement : 12 mois
ANDROTELO.Autres actes ajoutés par la recherche: Bilan pour l’évaluation thérapeutique, test de grossesse pour les femmes en âge de procréer à chaque visite et pour la tolérance du traitement s’ajoutant aux soins courants : une IRM et une échographie hépatique et splénique, une ostéodensitométrie, deux évaluations de la longueur des télomères (15 ml x2 de sang), un scanner thoracique et un EFR pour les patients avec atteinte hématologique), un myélogramme avec étude cytogénétique (frottis + 1 ml de moelle) pour les patients avec atteinte pulmonaire, trois dosages de l’alpha foeto- protéine (5ml de sang), et trois dosage des PSA (5ml de sang) pour les individus de sexe masculin, un bilan lipidique (5ml de sang) et un bilan hépatique (5 ml de sang).
ANDROTELO.Risques ajoutés par la recherche: Complications hépatiques cytolytiques ou cholestatiques, croissance de tumeurs androgéno- dépendantes.
ANDROTELO.Déroulement pratique: Après vérification des critères d’éligibilité et obtention du consentement éclairé du patient, le patient sera inclus avec des visites d’évaluations cliniques, biologiques +/- radiologiques à 1, 2, 3, 6, 9 et 12 mois. Le traitement à l’étude est prescrit tous les 3 mois jusqu’à 12 mois.

PACIFIC.Titre complet: Protection vaccinale Anti-Covid-19 portant sur les enfants Immunodéprimés (1 à 15 ans) atteints de leucémie aiguë et leur Fratrie (de 5 à15 ans). Essai de Phase I-II évaluant la tolérance et l’Immunogénicité humorale et Cellulaire post-vaccinale.
PACIFIC.Justification scientifique: La mortalité en cas d’infection à SARS-CoV-2 (Covid-19) en cours de traitement d’une leucémie aiguë (LA) est d’environ 30%, soit plus de 10 fois celle de la population générale. Des formes graves sont rapportées chez les enfants sous chimiothérapie pour LA. Néanmoins le risque principal, largement sous-estimé, est lié au retard d’exécution de la chimiothérapie en cas d’infection, les exposant à un risque majoré de rechute. Il est donc justifié de proposer une vaccination anti- Covid-19 chez ces patients. Une vaccination de l’entourage paraît également nécessaire compte-tenu des incertitudes sur la réponse vaccinale de l’enfant malade et du fait que le foyer familial est la principale source de contamination. Le vaccin à ARNm COMIRNATY® (BNT162b2) possède une AMM chez les individus de plus de 12 ans et vient d’obtenir l’autorisation d’utilisation chez l’enfant de 5 à 11 ans. Chez l’enfant immunodéprimé atteint de LA, les données de tolérance et d’efficacité sont inconnues. La balance bénéfice risque pèse pour une utilisation hors AMM du vaccin chez les enfants de 1 à 15 ans atteints de LA. Concernant l’entourage, la vaccination des parents et de la fratrie de plus de 12 ans est réalisée depuis plusieurs mois dans le cadre du soin et vient d’être recommandée pour les enfants de 5 à 11 ans vivant dans l’entourage des personnes immunodéprimées. Elle est ainsi également proposée à la fratrie de 5 à 15 ans dans le cadre du protocole.
PACIFIC.Objectif et critère d’évaluation princip: Evaluer la tolérance et l’immunogénicité du vaccin COMIRNATY® (BNT162b2) (deux injections à 21-28 jours d’intervalle) chez les enfants atteints de LA (1 à 15 ans) et leur fratrie (5 à 15 ans) Critères d’évaluation principaux : co-primary endpoints - Toxicité dose limitante (TDL) définie sur la présence dans les 7 jours après injection vaccinale d’un événement indésirable imputable au vaccin de grade 3 ou plus (détaillés en section 4.1.1) - Titre d’IgG anti-Spike ≥ 260 BAU/ml (Détection quantitative des anticorps anti-spike par technique de chimiluminescence ALINITY (Abbott)), 1 mois après la 2ème dose de vaccin. 1) Critères de tolérance La Toxicité dose limitante (TDL) est définie selon les critères mentionnés dans le Tableau 1. Ils sont dérivés de la CTCAE V5.0 (1) et du guide FDA « Toxicity Grading Scale for Healthy Adult and Adolescent Volunteers Enrolled in Preventive Vaccine Clinical Trials » (2). Tout autre événement indésirable clinique de grade 3-4 inattendu selon le CTCAE V5.0 en lien avec la vaccination. Un comité de relecture des évènements critiques et TDL validera si les EIG de grade 3-4 déclarés sont imputables aux vaccins. 2) Critères d’immunogénicité Le patient est considéré comme ayant une « séroconversion significative » s’il présente un titre d’IgG anti-Spike ≥ 260 BAU/ml (Détection quantitative des anticorps anti-spike par technique de chimiluminescence ALINITY (Abbott)), 1 mois après la 2ème dose de vaccin.

PACIFIC.Schéma expérimental: Essai de Phase I-II, bicentrique, chez les enfants atteints de LA et leur fratrie, avec recherche de la dose de vaccin bien tolérée selon l’âge basée sur un schéma bayesien et mesure de l’immunogénicité humorale et cellulaire. La recherche de dose utilisera un schéma 321 Bayesien décrit par Cunanan en 2017.
PACIFIC.Population concernée: - Enfants de 1 à 15 ans atteints de LA en cours de chimiothérapie ou dont la date de dernière séance de chimiothérapie est inférieure ou égale à 12 mois. - Fratrie des enfants atteints de LA (vivant sous le même toit > 50% du temps) : de 5 à 15 ans.
PACIFIC.Critères d’inclusion: - Enfant de 1 à 15 ans : • Atteint de leucémie aiguë lymphoblastique en cours de chimiothérapie (2 semaines au minimum après la dernière injection de PEG-ASPARAGINASE) ou dont la dernière chimiothérapie est inférieure ou égale à 12 mois. • OU Atteint de leucémie aiguë myéloïde au plus tard 12 mois après la fin du traitement - Frère ou sœur de 5 à 15 ans vivant sous le même toit que l’enfant atteint de LA plus de 50% du temps - Consentement éclairé des parents - Patient affilié à un régime de sécurité sociale - Pour les femmes en âge de procréer : o Un test sanguin négatif lors de la visite d’inclusion o ET utilisation d’une méthode contraceptive efficace au moins 4 semaines avant la vaccination et jusqu’au moins 12 semaines après la dernière vaccination
PACIFIC.Critères de non inclusion: - Infection documentée au SARS-CoV-2 en cours ou datant de moins de deux mois - Allergie clinique connue au polyéthylène glycol (PEG) - Taux de plaquettes < 50 G/L ou taux de PNN < 0.5G/L au moment de la vaccination - Vaccination en dehors de la grippe dans les 4 semaines précédant la première injection ou ayant prévu de recevoir un vaccin homologué 4 semaines après la dernière injection - Vaccination anti-grippe dans les 14 jours avant la 1ère injection - Tout trouble hémorragique considéré comme une contre- indication à l'injection intramusculaire - Antécédents d’effets indésirables sévères après l’administration d’un vaccin incluant une réaction anaphylactique et les symptômes associés, comme un rash, une difficulté respiratoire un angio-oedème et une douleur abdominale, ou des antécédents de réaction allergique pouvant être exacerbée par un composant du vaccin - Participant ayant été vacciné contre le BCG au cours de l'année précédente. - Participant malade ou fébrile (température corporelle ≥38°C) dans les 72 heures précédentes présentant des symptômes suggérant la présence de COVID-19. - Allergie à l’un des composants du vaccin ou antécédents allergiques graves (de type anaphylactique) - Traitement reçu pour une infection Covid-19 (60 jours avant 1ère injection). - Infection connue au VIH, au VHC ou au VHB - Utilisation d'Ig expérimentales, d'anticorps monoclonaux expérimentaux ou de sérum de convalescents anti-covid-19 dans les 90 jours avant l’entrée dans l’étude - Femme enceinte, allaitement en cours ou test de grossesse positif lors de la visite d'inclusion. - Participation à un essai sur la vaccination - Participation sans l’accord du médecin investigateur à une autre recherche dans les 4 semaines avant la visite d’inclusion et pendant la durée de l’essai
PACIFIC.Traitement(s) à l’essai: Vaccin COMIRNATY® (BNT162b2) : 2 injections à 21 jours d’intervalle

Prélèvements : - 10 à 15 ml à inclusion et à M2, M6, M12 pour la réalisation de l’Elispot à l’occasion d’une prise de sang réalisée dans le cadre du soin - 2 tubes de 2 ml (pour les sérologies) à l’inclusion, entre J21 et J28, M2 (+/- M3 chez les enfants n’ayant pas séconverti), M6 et M12 - 5 ml pour les AC neutralisants à J0, M2, M6 et M12 (+/- M3), - PCR SARS-CoV-2 nasopharyngée ou salivaire ou test antigénique à J8 du diagnostic en cas d’infection Covid-19, puis hebdomadaire jusqu’à négativation >> Chez les enfants sains : Consultations : Visites de sélection, d’inclusion (J0), de suivi à J7, entre J21 et J28, M2, M6 et M12 Prélèvements : - 5 ml pour la biologie standard - 15 ml à l’inclusion, à M2, M6 et M12 (pour la réalisation de l’Elispot) - 2 tubes de 2 ml (pour les sérologies) à l’inclusion, entre J21 et J28, M2, M6 et M12 - 5 ml pour les AC neutralisants à J0, M2, M6 et M12 - PCR SARS-CoV-2 nasopharyngée ou salivaire ou test antigénique à J8 du diagnostic en cas d’infection Covid-19 puis hebdomadaire jusqu’à négativation
PACIFIC.Bénéfices attendus pour les participants: - Réduction de l’incidence des formes graves de Covid-19 chez les enfants atteints de LA - Réduction du nombre de jours de retard au traitement induit par une infection au Covid-19 chez les enfants atteints de LA
PACIFIC.Risques ajoutés par la recherche: Les risques ajoutés par la recherche, liés aux actes/médicaments sont : 1) Risques liés au vaccin : - Réaction locale : gonflement au site d'injection ou gonflement étendu du membre vacciné plus rarement, rougeur au site d'injection, prurit au site d'injection, douleurs dans l’extrémité du bras vacciné - Réaction générale : frissons, fièvre, réactions d'hypersensibilité, céphalées, paralysie faciale périphérique aiguë, paresthésie, hypoesthésie, diarrhée, nausées, vomissements, arthralgies, myalgies, malaise, anxiété, myocardite, péricardite, lymphadénopathie, diminution de l’appétit, insomnies, léthargie, hyperhydrose, sueurs nocturnes, asthénie, érythème polymorphe, gonflement du visage, paralysie soudaine et temporaire des muscles d’un côté du visage entrainant un affaissement, sensation de faiblesse ou manque d’énergie/somnolence. 2) Risques liés à la ponction (prélèvement sanguin) : - Hématome au point de ponction - Douleur au point de ponction - Malaise - Anxiété Etude de risque D (classification APHP)
PACIFIC.Déroulement pratique: - Après signature du consentement éclairé, les sujets candidats feront l’objet d’une visite médicale d’inclusion, comprenant un interrogatoire, un examen clinique et un bilan biologique pour vérifier leur éligibilité. Le résultat de la PCR Covid-19 sera attendu avant administration du vaccin. - Pour tout sujet inclus, 2 doses du vaccin COMIRNATY® (BNT162b2 à J0 et J21-J28) seront administrées (sauf si TDL après 1ère dose). - Une 3ème dose est prévue pour les patients traités pour une leucémie aiguë, en l’absence de séroconversion à 2 mois de la 1ère injection. - Les patients atteints de LA seront stratifiés en 3 groupes d’âge : ≥1-<2 ans, ≥2-<5 ans, ≥5-<12 ans. Trois doses de vaccin ont été prédéfinies (10, 20, et 30 µg) pour évaluation chez les enfants atteints de LA de 1 à moins de 12 ans. Les enfants 12 ans et plus recevront la dose de 30 µg. - Une recherche de dose de vaccin maximale tolérée sera réalisée chez les enfants de moins de 12 ans atteints de LA. On utilisera le schéma 321 (Cunanan 2017) permettant d’estimer la dose tolérée pour chaque strate d’âge tout en tenant compte des événements observés entre cohortes selon un modèle hiérarchique. - Ce choix a été justifié par une préoccupation éthique afin de limiter les risques d’exposition des enfants à des niveaux trop toxiques. - Les frères et soeurs sains recevront 2 doses du vaccin COMIRNATY® (BNT162b2 à J0 et J21-J28) à la dose de 30 µg pour les 12 ans et plus, et à la dose de 10 µg pour les 5 à 11 ans selon les recommandations en vigueur.
PACIFIC.Nombre de sujets sélectionnés: 150 : - 100 patients atteints de LA (on vise 25 patients par groupe d’âge : ≥1-<2 ans, ≥2-<5 ans, ≥5-<12 ans pour la recherche de dose et 25 patients également chez les adolescents de 12-15 ans). Cependant tous les patients atteints de LA présentant les critères d’inclusion seront inclus dans l’essai dans leur strate sans limite de nombre par strate jusqu’à hauteur de 100 patients au total. - 50 sujets sains issus de la fratrie (5 à 15 ans)
PACIFIC.Nombre de centres: Bi-centrique : Centres de la SFCE (Société Française de lutte contre les cancers et leucémies de l’enfant et de l’adolescent). En France 01 : Armand Trousseau 02 : Robert Debré
PACIFIC.Durée de la recherche: Durée d’inclusion : 15 mois - Durée de participation (traitement + suivi) : 12 mois - Durée totale : 27 mois
PACIFIC.Nombre d’inclusions prévues par centre e: 3 à 4 patients / centre / mois 1 à 2 sujets sains / centre / mois
PACIFIC.Analyse statistique: Recherche de dose chez les enfants atteints de LA âgés de 12 ans ou moins Les analyses seront réalisées séquentiellement, stratifiées sur le groupe d’âge, et réalisées après chaque enfant. On se basera sur le schéma CRM. On se placera dans un contexte bayésien pour estimer les probabilités a posteriori de TDL (p), pour chaque niveau de dose, dans chaque classe d’âge.

ACTIVATE.Full title: Open label multi-center dose-escalation phase 1 Clinical Trial Assessing safety, tolerability and efficacy of the combination of Actinomycin D and venetoclax in Relapsed/Refractory (R/R) Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML)
ACTIVATE.Scientific justification: R/R AML is an unmet medical need. Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a heterogeneous clonal myeloid neoplasm where abnormal proliferation and impaired differentiation of hematopoietic stem and myeloid progenitor cells impede normal hematopoiesis. Despite the significant progress made in understanding AML oncogenesis over the past decades, this disease remains devastating with about 18,000 new cases every year in Europe and a five-year overall survival of only 17%1. The standard of care (SOC) of newly diagnosed AML includes a ‘7+3’ cytarabine-anthracyclin combination followed by repeated courses of high dose cytarabine with or without allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT)2. Up to one third of unselected AMLs are refractory to intensive chemotherapy. Outcome of such primary refractory AMLs is dismal, with a median survival shorter than one year3. Half of patients achieving a remission after intensive therapy eventually relapse. The majority of relapsed AMLs lack tractable FLT3 or IDH1-2 driver mutations and their treatment rely on intensive salvage therapy, with a minority of patients proceeding to a potentially curative HSCT4. Patients with newly diagnosed AML who are too old or frail for intensive chemotherapy receive less intensive therapies based on hypomethylating agents (HMAs), which, as single agents, are not curative5. Though the prognosis of such patients may improve in the coming decade with the addition of venetoclax to frontline HMAs6, patients relapsing or refractory to HMA-based therapies also have survival rates lower than 12 months7. As such, R/R AML represents an unmet medical need. Novel treatment options independent of the conventional chemotherapy and HMA backbones used in the frontline setting are thus necessary. Actinomycin D and Venetoclax show synergism in AML. In 2018, venetoclax received accelerated approval by the FDA for use in AML patients. As a BH3 mimetic, venetoclax is a selective and oral inhibitor that binds to BCL-2, an important regulator of the apoptosis pathway by tightly controlling the release of cytochrome C from the mitochondria, the initiating step during apoptosis8. Actinomycin D is known to inhibit RNA Polymerase I (RNA Pol I), depleting nucleoli of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and inducing nucleolar stress response in AML cells9. Actinomycin D has also been shown to repress MCL-1 expression and synergize with BH3 mimetics in cancer cell lines10. MCL-1 upregulation is a major venetoclax resistance pathway11. Lately, it has been shown that actinomycin D targets primed mitochondria in AML cell driving TP53 activation and senescence of AML cells. Based on the pharmacodynamics of these two drugs, pre-clinical data have demonstrated the synergistic effect of venetoclax and actinomycin D12. Actinomycin D as a single agent has been used in R/R AML and retrospective data published showed that four out of the nine evaluable patients achieved CR/CRi9; or that three out of 17 patients with morphologic relapses or refractory AML achieved complete morphologic remission (CR) after the first cycle of Actinomycin D13. Retrospective data about the actinomycin D-venetoclax combination in R/R AML are available with overall response rate ranges from 26%14 to 75%15. Interestingly, responses to the combination of ActD- Ven were also noted in patients previously exposed to venetoclax. Finally, no treatment-related death was reported in those retrospective series14,15. Collectively, these findings provide a strong rationale for the clinical evaluation of Actinomycine D-Venetoclax combination in R/R AML patients. The purpose of this phase 1 study is to evaluate the safety and feasibility of such strategy, provide preliminary signals of efficacy, and identify potential biomarkers.
ACTIVATE.Main objective and primary endpoint: Main objective: To identify the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of Actinomycin D / Venetoclax combination in patients with R/R AML. Primary endpoint: Dose Limiting Toxicity (DLT) DLT will be defined during a safety observation period corresponding to the first cycle of Actinomycin D/Venetoclax treatment, as: ● Death of any cause (with the exception of deaths caused by clear evidence of disease progression, defined as a leukocytosis greater than 50 × 10⁹/L) ● Prolonged myelosuppression on day 42 from start of therapy or later without evidence of leukemia defined by the absence of platelet recovery above 50 × 10⁹/L without transfusion support and the absence of neutrophil recovery with ANC > 1 × 10⁹/L ● Grade ≥ 3 non- hematological toxicity with the exception of: o Grade 3 or 4 infections o Grade 3 or 4 fever with neutropenia o Grade 3 nausea, vomiting or diarrhea that can be managed to ≤ Grade 2 within 72 hours of symptomatic treatment o Grade 3 mucositis or stomatitis that can be managed to ≤ Grade 2 within 72 hours of symptomatic treatment o Grade 3 tumor lysis syndrome that resolves within 72 hours of onset with medical treatment o Grade 3 or 4 hemorrhage Probability of DLT should not exceed 33% at the end of the first cycle of Actinomycin D/Venetoclax (Day 28-42).
ACTIVATE.Secondary objectives and endpoints: Secondary objectives: 1) To characterize safety of the combination Actinomycin D/ Venetoclax 2) To preliminarily assess the anti-leukemia efficacy of the combination of Actinomycin D/ Venetoclax treatment. 3) To assess the combined pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of Actinomycin D/ Venetoclax treatment in leukemia cells of peripheral blood and bone marrow. Secondary endpoints: 1) Safety evaluation ● AE, TEAE, treatment related TEAE, TEAES leading to treatment discontinuation, serious adverse events (SAE): Frequency, duration and severity ● Safety outcome measures will be assessed continuously during the study. ● Monitoring of ECGs and clinical laboratory values are integral to safety assessment. ● Adverse events (AE), treatment emergent adverse events (TEAE) and treatment-related TEAE will be evaluated according to the NCI CTCAE version 6.0. Serious adverse events will be defined per protocol according to EMA/ICH criteria. Causality relationship with the experimental treatment should be assessed by the investigator. ● Patients should be followed until all treatment related adverse event have returned to grade ≤ 1 or baseline or are deemed irreversible by the investigator. 2) Preliminary assessment of anti-leukemia efficacy ● Complete response rate including CR, CRi (CR with incomplete hematologic recovery, meaning CR with platelet count <100,000/µL or absolute neutrophil count <1000/µL) and CRh (CR with partial hematologic recovery, meaning CR not fulfilling CR or CRi peripheral blood count criteria but with platelet count >50,000/µL AND absolute neutrophil count >500/µL). ● Morphologic leukemia-free state (MLFS): blastic criteria of response on the bone marrow aspirate, absence of extramedullary disease and no requirement of hematologic recovery. ● Partial response (PR): absence of circulating blasts; absence of extramedullary disease; decrease of bone marrow blast percentage from 5 to 25% and decrease of pretreatment bone marrow blast percentage by at least 50% ● Overall response rate (ORR) being defined as CR, CRi and CRh, MLFS and PR rates. ● Event-free survival (EFS); here events are defined as: o Non achievement of hematologic response including CR, CRi, CRh o Hematologic relapse or progressive disease o Initiation of any subsequent anti-leukemic therapy (excluding hydroxyurea) o Deaths prior to one of the events mentioned above Reasons for subsequent therapy initiation (including intolerance, resistance, hematologic relapse, unsatisfactory MRD evolution), its type (intensive, less-intensive, best supportive care) and its frame (clinical trial, off-label or compassionate use) will be prospectively recorded. ● Progressive disease (PD): o >50% increase in marrow blasts over baseline (a minimum 15 points increase is required in cases with <30% blasts at baseline); or a persistent marrow blast percentage of >70% over at least 3 months, (without at least a 100% improvement in ANC to an absolute level >0.5x109/L and/or platelet count to > 50 x 109/L, non-transfused); o Or a new extramedullary disease ● Duration of response (DOR), ● Relapse free survival (RFS) ● Overall survival (OS) ● Early mortality rates after 1 cycle of treatment (day 28-42) and after 2 cycles (day 56-84) ● Incidence of subsequent allogeneic HSCT, overall and in responding patients specifically ● Molecular Residual Disease (MRD) will be evaluated as follow: Peripheral blood RQ-PCR for NPM1 patients16, BM RQ-PCR for t(8;21) and inv(16) patients17, otherwise FCM. Apart from specific mentions, all these hematological endpoints will be defined according to the last recommendation of the European Leukemia Network (ELN; currently the 2022 ELN recommendations in Döhner H et al Blood 2022). 3) Pharmacokinetics/Pharmacodynamics To assess the combined pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of Actinomycin D/Venetoclax treatment in leukemia cells of peripheral blood and bone marrow, during the clinical trial, with research of biomarkers of response
ACTIVATE.Design of the study: Dose-escalation phase 1, open label, multicenter clinical trial following an adaptive Bayesian time to event continual reassessment design (TITE-CRM), to identify the optimal schedule of Actinomycine D in combination with Venetoclax days 1-7. The design will be applied to a single, specific population: adult patients with a confirmed diagnosis of relapsed or refractory AML, regardless of prior treatments or number of relapses. Number of Samples: 36 patients in total
ACTIVATE.Population of study participants: Patients aged 18 years old or more with R/R AML.
ACTIVATE.Inclusion criteria: ● Patients aged 18 years old or more ● Patients with confirmed diagnosis of R/R AML according to the 2022 ELN recommendations who have failed available standard therapies, are not eligible for standard therapeutic options, or for whom no appropriate standard treatment option is considered available according to the investigator’s judgment ● WBC < 20,000/mm3 (previous HY is allowed to control WBC count) ● ECOG performance status ≤2 ● Any prior treatment-related toxicities resolved to ≤ Grade 1 prior to first study dose, with the exception of ≤ Grade 2 neuropathy or alopecia ● AST and ALT ≤3.0 x upper the limit of normal (ULN) and total and direct serum bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN unless considered due to leukemia, in which case thresholds may be increased to ≤ 6.0 × ULN for transaminases and ≤ 3.0 × ULN for bilirubin. ● Estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) ≥ 50 mL/min/1,73m2 according to the MDRD equation ● Posaconazole prophylaxis for invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA) ● Written informed consent obtained prior to any screening procedures ● Patients affiliated or beneficiary of the National Health Insurance in France (AME excluded)
ACTIVATE.Exclusion criteria: - Acute promyelocytic leukemia - Proven central nervous system leukemic involvement - Prior allogeneic HSCT within the last 12 weeks or donor lymphocyte conditioning (DLI) within the last 4 weeks - Graft-Versus-Host Disease (GVHD): Signs or symptoms of acute GVHD ≥ Grade 2, moderate or severe limited chronic GVHD or extensive chronic GVHD of any severity within the last 4 weeks prior to the first study dose. Patients must have been off all systemic immunosuppressive therapy for at least 2 weeks prior to enrollment. Patients may receive as GVHD treatment corticosteroid doses ≤ 10 mg of prednisone daily. - Concurrent therapy with any cytotoxic drug within 3 weeks before the first study dose. Only hydroxyurea for the control of blood counts is permitted. - Adults weighting less than 40 kg - Uncontrolled systemic fungal, bacterial, or viral infection (defined as ongoing signs/symptoms related to the infection without improvement despite appropriate treatment) - HBV or HCV hepatitis with a detectable viral load or any ongoing anti-viral treatment - HIV with a detectable viral load or any ongoing anti-viral treatment - Other uncontrolled or active malignant disease within prior 12 months (excluding myelodysplastic syndrome; myeloproliferative neoplasm, cutaneous basal cell carcinoma, “in-situ” carcinoma of the cervix or breast, or other local malignancy excised) - Inability to swallow - Known malabsorption syndrome or other condition that may significantly impair absorption of oral study medications - Administration of any therapy that is considered to be investigational (i.e., used for non-approved indications(s) or in the context of a research investigation) within 3 weeks or 5 drug half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to the first dose of study drug - Any concurrent severe and/or uncontrolled medical condition, which could compromise participation in the study - Adult subjects to a legal protection order or unable to give their consent (tutelle, curatelle, sauvegarde de justice, habilitation familiale, mandate de protection future) - Persons deprived of their freedom by judicial or administrative decision, person hospitalized without their consent by virtues of articles L 3212-1 and L3213-1 and who are not subject to the provisions of article L 1121-8 - Females who are pregnant or breastfeeding - For males whose sexual partner is a woman of childbearing potential: unwillingness or inability of the man or woman to use a highly effective contraceptive method for the entire treatment period and for at least 6 months after completion of protocol treatment - For heterosexually active woman of childbearing potential: unwillingness or inability to use a highly effective contraceptive method for the entire treatment period and for at least 6 months after the administration of the final dose of study medication - Known allergies to investigational drug or to Posaconazole and/or excipients - Concomitant administration of St. John's Wort or yellow fever vaccine. Highly effective contraception methods include: combined (estrogen and progestogen containing) or progestogen-only hormonal methods associated with inhibition of ovulation, intra-uterine device, surgical sterilization (including bilateral tubal occlusion, partner’s vasectomy), or sexual abstinence if this is the preferred and usual lifestyle of the patient. In accordance with the venetoclax SmPC, women using hormonal contraception must also use an additional barrier contraceptive method during treatment and for the applicable post- treatment contraception period Women are not regarded as of childbearing potential if they are post- menopausal (at least 2 years without menses) or are surgically sterile (at least 1 month before enrolment). Female patients must not donate or retrieve, for their own use, ova from the time of screening and throughout the treatment period, and for 12 weeks after the administration of the final dose of study medication. Female patients must agree not to breastfeed from the time of screening and throughout the protocol period, and for (5 half-lives) days after the administration of the final dose of study medication. Male patients must not freeze or donate sperm starting at screening and throughout the treatment period and 3 months after the administration of the final dose of study medication.
ACTIVATE.caInvestigational medicinal product(s): Treatment will be delivered in consecutive cycles of 28 days of administration. Cycle windows may be extended beyond D28 upon prolonged myelosuppression, for monitoring until recovery. Patients will receive for two cycles: - Venetoclax daily days 1-7, - And Actinomycin D by short IV infusion 12.5 μg/kg/d for up to 3 days starting on D3. Patients deriving clinical benefit (defined as achievement of MLFS, CRi, CRh or CR) after 2 cycles may receive up to 10 consolidation cycles outside of the study, at the investigator's discretion, consisting of: - Venetoclax daily days 1-7, - And Actinomycin D by short IV infusion 12.5 μg/kg/d at day 3. Patients with a clinical benefit eligible for allogeneic transplantation, at the investigator's discretion, may receive up to 6 cycles prior to transplantation, outside of the study. Dose Levels for Actinomycin D are based on protocol available with safety data15 in keeping with FDA guidance for the co-development of two drugs18. Actinomycin D will start on d3, after initial ramp up dosage of venetoclax, up to 3 days. Venetoclax will be given with a ramp up dosage over 3 days (20-50- 70mg) until the daily dose of 70mg/d in patient with azole antifungal prophylaxis starting at D1. Venetoclax is given until D7 in each cycle to avoid further hematological toxicity. Three dose schedules of actinomycin D will be explored in induction phase, starting at DL1: • DL1: Venetoclax daily days 1-7 and Actinomycin D 12.5 μg/kg/d at day 3, • DL2: Venetoclax daily days 1-7 and Actinomycin D 12.5 μg/kg/d at days 3-4, • DL3: Venetoclax daily days 1-7 and Actinomycin D 12.5 μg/kg/d at days 3-5, Dose escalation will be conducted according to a dose finding design with sequential dose assignment with cohorts of size 3, the number of patients eventually assessed at each dose level depending on the DLT.

ACTIVATE.Expected benefits for the participants a: The ACTIVATE trial aims to provide new therapeutic options for patients with relapsed/refractory AML, a population with limited treatment alternatives and poor prognosis. Participants in the study may benefit from potentially improved response rates. The combination of Actinomycin D and Venetoclax has shown synergistic anti-leukemic effects, which could lead to higher remission rates and prolonged survival. Furthermore, identifying biomarkers of response may contribute to personalized medicine approaches, optimizing treatment strategies for future patients. On a broader scale, this trial could expand the therapeutic landscape for R/R AML, potentially leading to new standard-of-care treatment options and improved patient outcomes worldwide.
ACTIVATE.Risks and burdens added by the study: Participation in the ACTIVATE trial introduces potential risks and burdens associated with the investigational treatment. Actinomycin D and Venetoclax can cause hematologic toxicities, including prolonged myelosuppression, neutropenia, and thrombocytopenia, which may increase the risk of infections and bleeding complications. Non-hematologic toxicities of Actinomycine D such as gastrointestinal disturbances (nausea, diarrhea, mucositis) are also expected. Patients will require frequent hospital visits and hospitalization, laboratory assessments, bone marrow aspiration increasing the overall burden. The potential for tumor lysis syndrome (TLS) necessitates strict hydration protocols and prophylactic measures. Despite these risks, the study is designed to closely monitor adverse effects and adjust dosing as needed to maximize patient safety. ➔ D risk level study (very high level of risk)

EXPORAKT.Full title: Open-label multi-center Phase 1/2 Clinical Trial Assessing safety, tolerability and efficacy of the combination of Capivasertib and Selinexor in Relapsed/Refractory (R/R) Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML)
EXPORAKT.Scientific justification: R/R AML is an unmet medical need. Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a heterogeneous clonal myeloid neoplasm where abnormal proliferation and impaired differentiation of hematopoietic stem and myeloid progenitor cells impedes normal hematopoiesis. Despite the significant progress made in understanding AML oncogenesis over the past decades, this disease remains devastating with about 18,000 new cases every year in Europe and a five- year overall survival lower than 30%(1). The standard of care (SOC) of newly diagnosed AML includes a ‘7+3’ cytarabine-anthracyclin combination followed by repeated courses of high dose cytarabine with or without allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT)(2). Up to one third of unselected AMLs are refractory to intensive chemotherapy. Outcome of such primary refractory AMLs is dismal, with a median survival shorter than one year (3). Half of patients achieving a remission after intensive therapy eventually relapse. The majority of relapsed AMLs lack tractable FLT3 or IDH1-2 driver mutations and their treatment rely on intensive salvage therapy, with a minority of patients proceeding to a potentially curative HSCT (4). Patients with newly diagnosed AML too old or frail for intensive chemotherapy receive less intensive therapies based on hypomethylating agents (HMAs), which, as single agents, are not curative (5).Though the prognosis of such patients may improve in the coming decade with the addition of venetoclax to frontline HMAs (6), patients relapsing or refractory to HMA-based therapies also have survival rates lower than 12 months (7). As such, R/R AML represents an unmet medical need. Novel treatment options independent of the conventional chemotherapy and HMA backbones used in the frontline setting are thus necessary. Selinexor as a single agent is active in AML. Selinexor is a selective orally bioavailable inhibitor of the karyopherin XPO1/CRM1 that facilitates nuclear export of over 200 proteins, including tumor suppressors, transcription factors and cell cycle regulators. Selinexor was recently granted FDA accelerated approval for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma treatment (NCT02336815) (8). In AML, selective inhibitors of nuclear export (SINE) have shown potent anti- leukemic effects in multiple in vitro and in vivo models (9–11). Selinexor was first evaluated clinically in R/R AML and unfit elderly patients in a dose-escalation phase I study, showing modest efficacy as a single agent (9% CR/CRi, median OS: 2.7 months, NCT01607892) (12). The recommended phase 2 dose was 60 mg flat dose (~35 mg/m2) twice weekly. The activity of Selinexor was also assessed in combination with the HMA decitabine (32% CR/CRi, median OS 5.9 months, NCT02093403)(13), and with the standard of care “3+7” chemotherapeutic regimen (53% CR/CRi, median OS: 10.3 months, NCT02403310)(14). Both studies confirmed the tolerability profile of Selinexor in an AML population. The most common grade ≥ 3 adverse events (AEs) were febrile neutropenia, diarrhea, hyponatremia, thrombocytopenia, anemia and fatigue. Possible class-specific, unusual AEs included hyponatremia and blurred vision, but these were mostly grade 1-2 and self-limiting. Overall, these trials validated the safety and tolerability of Selinexor in AML patients, both as a single agent or in combination with AML SOCs. They prompt further clinical research efforts towards more clinically effective novel therapeutic combination studies. Capivasertib is safe in patients with solid tumors. AKT is encoded by three closely related genes (AKT1, AKT2 and AKT3) and is the central node of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR network, at the interface of oncogenic signaling and cancer metabolism (15). AKT is frequently activated in solid tumors, thus representing a promising target (15). Capivasertib is a potent, selective orally bioavailable ATP-competitive inhibitor of all 3 AKT isoforms (pan-AKT inhibitor). Capivasertib was evaluated in a dose escalation phase I trial in patients with advanced solid tumors (NCT01226316)(16). The recommended phase II dose (RP2D) was 480mg twice daily for 4 days followed by 3 days off within each week. The most frequently reported grade ≥ 2 AEs were hyperglycemia, diarrhea and nausea. Most AEs were managed with supportive care or dose reductions and no deaths related to Capivasertib were reported. Capivasertib has since been evaluated in combination with standard of care therapeutic agents in multiple phase I/II studies in solid tumors with frequent PI3K/AKT pathway activation such as breast and prostate cancer (NCT01226316, NCT02338622, NCT02525068)(17–19). These studies confirmed the tolerability profile of Capivasertib. Several phase III studies are ongoing to evaluate capivasertib efficacy in breast and prostate cancer (NCT03997123, NCT04493853). There is currently no clinical data regarding administration of capivasertib in AML patients, or regarding combination of capivasertib with SINEs such as Selinexor, regardless of disease. AKT inhibitors and selinexor show strong synergism in multiple pre- clinical models of AML. Using unbiased large scale functional genomic and proteomic screening approaches, inhibition of AKT was identified as a strong sensitizer to Selinexor in AML cell lines (PIs KC Wood, Duke University Durham, NC & A. Puissant, INSERM, Paris France) (20,21). Mechanistically, exposure of AML cells to single-agent selinexor was shown to induce an on-target, pro- oncogenic activation of the PI3K/AKT signaling, thus mitigating the anti- leukemic activity of Selinexor. Such AKT activation driven by Selinexor exposure contrasts with the low basal AKT levels in AML(22), and creates a therapeutic window for a synthetic lethal combination of Selinexor with pan-AKT inhibitors. Indeed, a strong synergism between Selinexor and pan-AKT inhibitors was observed in a panel of 5 AML cell lines with diverse genetic backgrounds, including difficult to treat subsets (eg KMT2A fusions, FLT3 mutations). This was confirmed with ex vivo treatment of cells from a patient-derived xenograft (PDX) model harboring high-risk mutations (RUNX1, ASXL1, EZH2, TET2) reminiscent of secondary-type AML, a frequent and challenging subtype of AML of the elderly(23). The synergistic anti-leukemic activity of pan-AKT inhibitor/selinexor combination was validated in vivo in multiple AML models, including xenotransplanted cell lines, syngeneic and PDX mouse models. In all models, combined treatment with Selinexor 15 mg/kg and the pan-AKT inhibitor Ipatasertib 65 mg/kg every other day for a total of 4 or 5 doses in mice with overt disease combination significantly reduced leukemic burden and improved survival compared to either drug alone or vehicle. Of note, both drugs showed limited but detectable single-agent activity over vehicle, though the magnitude of Ipatasertib potency was lower than that of Selinexor at the tested concentrations, and well below that of the combination. Importantly, the anti-leukemic effect of this novel combination was superior to the standard of care AML chemotherapeutic regimen in an aggressive syngeneic AML mouse model driven by the Mll- Af9 fusion. Compared to a ‘5+3’ regimen of cytarabine-anthracyclin, representing the MTD of SOC chemotherapy in this AML model, pan-AKT inhibitor / Selinexor combination led to prolonged survival. Finally, in a secondary transplantation study in limit dilution, pan-AKT inhibition combined to Selinexor led to a ~30-fold reduction in relapse-initiating leukemic stem cells over this SOC chemotherapy regimen. Collectively, these pre-clinical findings provide a strong rationale for the clinical evaluation of Capivasertib-Selinexor combination in R/R AML patients. The purpose of this phase 1/2 study is to evaluate the safety and feasibility of such strategy, provide preliminary signals of efficacy, and identify potential biomarkers.
EXPORAKT.Main objective and primary endpoint: Main Objectives Phase 1: To assess the safety of the combination of Capivasertib (Capiva) and Selinexor (Sel) in patients with R/R AML, characterizing the dose- limiting toxicities (DLTs), and identifying the maximal tolerated doses combination (MTDC) and recommended phase 2 doses combination. Phase 2: To assess preliminarily anti-leukemia efficacy of the combination of Capiva and Sel, in R/R AML with reference from historical data on single-agent Selinexor activity (lower threshold for meaningful activity 20% ORR)(12) while monitoring the safety profile of the treatment. Primary endpoint: Phase 1: Dose Limiting Toxicity (DLT) DLT will be defined during a safety observation period corresponding to the first cycle of 28 days of Capiva/sel treatment, or within 42 days of the first dose of study treatment (for Grade ≥ 3 neutropenia and thrombocytopenia only), as: ● Prolonged treatment-related Grade ≥ 3 neutropenia and/or Grade ≥ 3 thrombocytopenia lasting for 6 weeks or more from start of therapy without evidence of leukemia or underlying myelodysplastic syndrome ● Grade ≥ 3 non- hematological toxicity with the exception of: o Grade 3 or 4 infection o Grade 3 or 4 fever with neutropenia o Grade 3 nausea, vomiting or diarrhea that can be managed to ≤ Grade 2 within 72 hours of symptomatic treatment o Grade 3 hyponatremia that can be managed to ≤ Grade 2 within 72 hours of symptomatic treatment o Grade 3 hyperglycemia that can be managed to ≤ Grade 2 within 72 hours of symptomatic treatment o Grade 3 hyperlipidemia that can be managed to ≤ Grade 2 within ≤ 2 weeks of symptomatic treatment o Grade 3 tumor lysis syndrome that improves to ≤ Grade 2 within 72 hours of onset with medical treatment o Any Grade ≥ 3 asymptomatic laboratory abnormalities that improves to ≤ Grade 2 within 72 hours o Anorexia or fatigue RP2DC can be equal to or one dose level lower than a MTDC. The choice of Combination Dose Level will depend on DSMB recommendations based on safety data (1 or >1 combinations recommended by the dose finding design), PK/PD data and efficacy signals from Phase 1. Phase 2: Co-primary endpoints - Overall response rate at 28 days according to the last recommendation of the European Leukemia Network (ELN; currently the 2022 ELN recommendations)(26), defined as any of the following: complete response (CR, CRi (CR with incomplete hematologic recovery, meaning CR with platelet count <100,000/µL or absolute neutrophil count <1000/µL),CRh (CR with partial hematologic recovery, meaning CR not fulfilling CR or CRi peripheral blood count criteria but with platelet count >50,000/µL AND absolute neutrophil count >500/µL)), MLFS (Morphologic leukemia-free state: blastic criteria of response on the bone marrow aspirate, absence of extramedullary disease and no requirement of hematologic recovery), and Partial response (PR): absence of circulating blasts; absence of extramedullary disease; decrease of bone marrow blast percentage to 5 to 25% and decrease of pretreatment bone marrow blast percentage by at least 50%). - Dose Limiting Toxicity (DLT), within 28 days, as defined above

Exploratory objectives To assess the combined pharmacodynamics of Capiva/Sel in leukemia cells of peripheral blood and bone marrow, during both phases of the clinical trial. To identify potential biomarkers of response. Exploratory endpoints 1) Pharmacodynamics ● XPO1 mRNA and protein expression by RQ-PCR and Western Blot of PBMCs/BMNCs ● P2RY2 and TP53 mRNA expression by RQ-PCR of PBMCs/BMNCs, ● AKT protein expression and phosphorylation levels of threonine 308 (Thr308) and serine 473 (Ser473) by Western-Blot. pAKT Thr308 levels will also be evaluated by flow-cytometry in BMNCs ● pS6, pPRAS40 by Western-Blot in BMNCs ● FOXO nuclear localization in BMNCs ● phosphorylated GSK3β (pGSK3β) in PRP ● insulin, glucose, and c-peptide levels in blood samples ● exploratory: RPPA in selected patients (responders/non responders) in BMNCs 2) Biomarkers of response • Cytogenetic analysis • Targeted sequencing including recurrent AML drivers and PI3K pathway genes
EXPORAKT.Design of the study: Phase 1/2, open label, multicenter clinical trial with two subsequent phases: Phase 1: dose-escalation with a Bayesian adaptive dose escalation design for drug combination, the product of independent beta probabilities dose escalation (PIPE) phase I design (27), to identify the maximal tolerated dose defined only for contour and recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). The time-to-event extension of the PIPE design may be used depending on the anticipated accrual rate compared to the DLT observation window (observation window 28 days) (28). Phase 1 will be conducted in patients with R/R AML agnostic of genetic mutation status. Phase 2: Extension at the MTDC or at the RP2DC chosen by the data and safety monitoring board (DSMB), to confirm the safety of RP2DC and preliminarily document its clinical efficacy. A Bayesian adaptive design will be used, assessing response probability (overall response rate) and monitoring toxicity (29). The design will include futility and safety decision rules (interim and final). Inclusion will be stratified on the TP53 status to ensure a maximum 20% patient with mutated TP53 (n=4 for a phase 2 sample of 20 patients).
EXPORAKT.Population of study participants: Patients aged 18 years old or more with R/R AML

EXPORAKT.Investigation al medicinal product(s): Patients will receive Selinexor and Capivasertib per os (tablets) in consecutive cycles of 28 days, until disease progression, death or consent withdrawal. The study treatment period will continue for up to 24 cycles after the first dose of study drug of the last enrolled patient. Patients who continue to benefit beyond 24 cycles according to investigator’s judgment could be enrolled in a subsequent extended treatment access study as part of a protocol amendment if Astrazeneca and Menarini agree to continue drug delivery for these patients. Selinexor is approved and marketed as treatment of multiple myeloma. Capivasertib is evaluated in phase 3 trials in breast and prostate cancer. Dose Levels for Selinexor and Capivasertib are based on RP2D and available safety data(12,16), in keeping with FDA guidance for the co- development of two drugs(30). Selinexor tablets dosed at 20mg, capivasertib tablets dosed at 80mg, 160mg or 200mg. Selinexor will be given at 40mg, 60mg or 80mg once weekly at D1, 8, 15, and 22 of 28-days cycles. Capivasertib will be given at 240, 320, 400 or 480 mg once daily, D1-4, 8- 11, 15-18, 22-25, of 28-days cycles. Eight candidate drug doses combinations will be evaluated: ● Combination DL-1: 40 mg Selinexor, 240mg Capivasertib. ● Combination DL-2: 40 mg Selinexor, 320mg Capivasertib. ● Combination DL-3: 60 mg Selinexor, 320mg Capivasertib. ● Combination DL-4: 60 mg Selinexor, 400mg Capivasertib. ● Combination DL-5: 60 mg Selinexor, 480mg Capivasertib. ● Combination DL-6: 80 mg Selinexor, 320mg Capivasertib. ● Combination DL-7: 80 mg Selinexor, 400mg Capivasertib. ● Combination DL-8: 80 mg Selinexor, 480mg Capivasertib. Dose escalation will be conducted according to a dose finding design with sequential dose assignment with cohorts of size 1 to 3, the number of patients eventually assessed at each dose level depending on the DLT observations.

EXPORAKT.Expected benefits for the participants a: Foreseeable benefits are the identification of the most efficient and less toxic dose level combination of Capivasertib/Selinexor. This novel therapeutic strategy should result in improvement of the complete response, overall response rates and long-term outcomes of R/R AML patients.
EXPORAKT.Practical implementati on: Consecutive eligible patients will be included following informed consent. This is a Phase 1/2, open-label, multicenter clinical trial with two consecutive phases (patients will participate in either Phase 1 or Phase 2): Phase 1: Bayesian adaptive dose escalation scheme for the combination of two drugs in patients with relapsed or refractory AML, irrespective of their molecular abnormalities. This part will be multicentric, with 3 CLIP2-INCa accredited centers. Phase 2: extension at the MTD or recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) after consulting the independent Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB), to confirm the safety of RP2D and document its clinical anti-leukemic activity on a preliminary basis. This phase will be multicentric (5 centers).

EXPORAKT.Statistical analysis: Bayesian adaptive designs will be used for the trial objectives. They allow sequential monitoring of data during the trial, using all current evidence for straightforward inference on safety and efficacy and decision making to select and evaluate an optimal dose. Phase 1 A product of independent beta probabilities dose escalation phase I design will be used in phase 1, for up to 24 patients (27). Target DLT rate for the definition of the MTD contour (MTC) will be 20%, across the dosing grid including 8 candidate drug doses combinations, defined by 3 candidate dose levels of Selinexor and 4 of Capivasertib (see section Investigational Medicinal Products). A time-to-event extension design may be used depending on the anticipated accrual rate compared to the DLT observation window (observation window 28 days) (28). The design will be calibrated (beta priors, escalation strategy, cohort size and safety constraints) to ensure coherence of the dose escalation scheme and obtain desirable operating characteristics (notably, probability of correct MTC selection, probability of overdose selection, safety of treatment assignments during the trial). Phase 2 Once phase 1 has been completed providing the estimated MTD, an extension of up to 44 patients will be initiated. Assuming 24 patients have been included in the phase 1 part of the study, 20 new patients will be included in the phase 2 part. The extension will follow a Bayesian adaptive design, assessing the probability of response (overall response rate) and monitoring toxicity (29). The choice of Dose Level for the extension phase will depend on DSMB recommendations based on safety data (1 or >1 combinations recommended by the dose finding design) and efficacy signals from Phase 1. Inclusion criteria will be similar as in Phase 1. Using the Bayesian Optimal Phase 2 design (BOP2) (29), a maximum total of 20 patients, with an interim analysis on the first 9 observations with futility and toxicity decision rules, allows 80% power given a 5% one-sided false positive rate (31), assuming a 10% response rate as unacceptable and 40% as desirable, while a limiting toxicity rate of 40% will be considered as unacceptable and 20 % as acceptable (as in the phase 1 part). We assume independent response and toxicity rates. Among the first 9 patients, if no response has been observed (no. response=0) or if 4 or more limiting toxicities have been observed, the trial will be stopped. Otherwise (if at least 1 response and no more than 3 limiting toxicities), accrual will resume up to a maximum of 20 patients in this part. At the second analysis, we will reject the undesirable hypothesis and conclude to a promising treatment if ≥4 responses are observed overall with ≤6 toxicities. Of note, inclusion in the phase II part will be stratified on the TP53 status to ensure a maximum 20% patient with mutated TP53 (n=4 for a phase 2 sample of 20 patients)

CAPTiRALL.Scientific justification: Tisagenlecleucel (CTL019) is an anti-CD19 autologous Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, which has shown dramatic early results in advanced ALLs. Early loss of B-cell aplasia (recovery of B-cells in marrow/ peripheral blood within 6 months after infusion), a marker of the loss or non-functionality of the CAR T- cells, is associated to a very high risk of relapse. A reinfusion of CTL019, even after Fludarabine- Cyclophosphamide reconditioning, frequently fails to induce further expansion as observed in UPENN studies and in the Robert Debré Hospital experience. Non-persistence of CAR T-cells may be due to immune- mediated rejection or environment-mediated suppression of their growth. Evidence for increased PD- 1 expression in CAR T-cells between infusion and peak expansion has been demonstrated in clinical samples. Preclinical data and few clinical data support a role of PD- 1–PD-L1 blockade in improving the effectiveness of CAR T-cell therapy. Tisagenlecleucel (CTL019) is an anti-CD19 autologous Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy which has shown dramatic early results in advanced ALLs. Early loss of B- cell aplasia (recovery of B-cells in marrow/ peripheral blood within 6 months after infusion), a marker of the loss or non- functionality of the CAR T-cells, is associated to a very high risk of relapse. A reinfusion of CTL019, even after Fludarabine- Cyclophosphamide reconditioning, frequently fails to induce further expansion as observed in UPENN studies and in the Robert Debré Hospital experience. Currently, there is no consensus for management of these patients who are at high risk of relapse. Different strategies are used depending on physician decision: clinical monitoring, allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, 2nd infusion of tisagenlecleucel or other. Here we would like to register prospectively patients who lost B-Cell aplasia within 6 months after 1st infusion to evaluate the eligibility rate of the CAPTiRALL trial evaluating the combination of an anti PD1 treatment and a second tisagenlecleucel infusion, and to describe the follow-up of patients presenting an early loss of B-cell aplasia and receiving the best current medical care.
CAPTiRALL.Main objectives and primary endpoint: To determine the safety, efficacy and feasibility of Nivolumab (Opdivo®)- an anti-PD1 treatment- combined to tisagenlecleucel in a cohort of relapsed or refractory B-ALL patients, aged 1-25 years old, previously treated by tisagenlecleucel (Kymriah®), with a demonstrated early loss of B-cell aplasia (within 6 months), a surrogate marker of the loss of CAR T-cells or their non- functionality. More specifically, the main objectives are: • In cohort 1 that includes patients with a MRD negative disease status combined to an early loss (within 6 months) of B-cell aplasia To determine the optimal starting time of Nivolumab (Opdivo®) in terms of safety and efficacy among 4 candidate time points (day 14, day 11, day 5, and day - 1). • In cohort 2 that includes relapsed patients with an early loss (within 6 months) of B-cell aplasia To estimate the feasibility in terms of safety and efficacy of a very early start of nivolumab (day-1), prior to the reinfusion of tisagenlecleucel These objectives will be evaluated on the two following co-primary endpoints: 1.1 Limiting-toxicities*** between infusion and D28 1.2 Efficacy, which evaluation is delayed at M3 after tisagenlecleucel reinfusion and defined by MRD negative CR* AND B cell aplasia** (*) MRD negative CR: undetectable disease at a 10-4 sensitivity threshold (**) B cell aplasia is defined by blood B lymphocytes < 10 /mm3 (or/and < 3% of total lymphocytes) (***) Limiting toxicities are defined at day 28 after tisagenlecleucel infusion, by the occurrence of either o Related to CAR-T cells infusion: • CRS or aGVH: limiting toxicity will be defined as toxicity ≥ 4 • ICANs: limiting toxicity will be defined as toxicity ≥ 3 (excepted grade 3 seizure, ie focal, generalized seizure that resolves rapidly) o Related to nivolumab: immune related myocarditis, pneumonitis, encephalitis: limiting toxicity will be defined as toxicity ≥ 4
CAPTiRALL.Secondary objectives and endpoints: Secondary endpoints: To assess the effect of these combined treatments on • Incidence of B cell aplasia at 6 months • Increase of B cell aplasia duration compared to the previous one observed after the first infusion of tisagenlecleucel (up to 24 months). • Disease best response • Complete remission (at M1 M3 M6 M12 after reinfusion) • Minimal residual disease (at M1 M3 M6 M12 after reinfusion) • 1-year OS • 1-year EFS • Incidence of Grade 3 adverse up to 2 years events such as - nivolumab-related adverse events: myocarditis, pneumonitis, encephalitis - tisagenlecleucel reinfusion-related events, in particular CRS or ICANs or aGVH, prolonged cytopenias • Incidence of Grade 3, 4 or 5 nivolumab-related adverse events up to 2 years: gut, liver, endocrine, stomatitis, rash or hematologic toxicity • Incidence of GVHD up to one year Exploratory endpoints: Long term efficacy: 2-year OS and EFS To explore the PD1 PDL1 axis and its correlation with success or failure To register minimal medical data for all patients with relapsed or refractory B-ALL, aged 1-25 years old, previously treated by tisagenlecleucel (Kymriah®), with a demonstrated early loss of B-cell aplasia* within 6 months, a surrogate marker of the loss of CAR T-cells or their non-functionality. *B cell aplasia is defined by blood B lymphocytes < 10 /mm3 (and/or < 3% of total lymphocytes) More specifically we will register medical decision according to physician, (ie, clinical monitoring, allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, 2nd infusion of tisagenlecleucel or other) for each included patient and patient’s disease status at the end of follow up.
CAPTiRALL.Design of the trial: This is a phase I/II clinical trial conducted in children, adolescents, and young adults with ALL, stratified on the disease status (marrow MRD negative or CD19+ relapse of B-cell ALL). Patients included first receive a lympho-depleting chemotherapy by Fludarabine / Cyclophosphamide. tisagenlecleucel infusion should then be administered 2 to 14 days after completion of chemotherapy. Nivolumab (Opdivo®) will be given intravenously at 3mg/kg every 2 weeks. 1) In the main cohort (cohort 1), i.e., in patients with MRD negative disease status: Time to Event Continual Reassessment Method (TITE-CRM) design a. Four decreasing starting times for beginning nivolumab (day 14, day 11, day 5 and day - 1) will be available for testing b. Patients will be enrolled sequentially by cohorts of 3 with escalation between cohorts based only on the limiting toxicities*** between infusion and D28 2) For relapsed patients (cohort 2): Pilot trial, with nivolumab starting at day -1. 3) In the main cohort (cohort 1), i.e., in patients with MRD negative disease status: Time to Event Continual Reassessment Method (TITE-CRM) design a. Four decreasing starting times for beginning nivolumab (day 14, day 11, day 5 and day -1) will be available for testing b. Patients will be enrolled sequentially by cohorts of 3 with escalation between cohorts based only on the limiting toxicities*** between infusion and D28 4) For relapsed patients (cohort 2): Pilot trial, with nivolumab starting at day -1. Nivolumab will be given until 12 months after tisagenlecleucel infusion in case of response. (***) Limiting toxicities are defined by the occurrence of any non- haematological targeted adverse events: o Related to CAR-T cells infusion: • CRS or aGVH: limiting toxicity will be defined as toxicity ≥ 4 • ICANs: limiting toxicity will be defined as toxicity ≥ 3 (excepted grade 3 seizure, ie focal, generalized seizure that resolves rapidly) Related to nivolumab: immune related myocarditis, pneumonitis, encephalitis: limiting toxicity will be defined as toxicity ≥ 4

CAPTiRALL.Grade 3/4 Neurological Toxicity: Discontinue protocol therapy • Obtain neurology consult • Treat symptoms per local guidelines • 1-2 mg/kg/day methylprednisolone IV or IV equivalent • Consider prophylactic anti infectious treatment for opportunistic infections

DualCALM-01.Scientific justification: Relapsed/refractory ALL represents an area of greatest unmet medical need. Second generation autologous anti CD19 CAR-T cells have shown promising results in terms of complete remission rates and relapse-free survival (RFS). Several mechanisms have been shown to lead to the loss of CD19 antigen expression and escape of anti CD19 CAR-T cells therapy. CD22 is observed in more than 90% of BCP-ALL and is already known as an interesting target. Targeting both CD19 and CD22 with our dual CAR-T could enhance CAR-T cells activity and limit tumour escape.
DualCALM-01.Main objective and primary endpoint: Main objective The primary objective of this clinical trial is to answer one key question in each phase: Phase I: To determine the DLT of MB-CART2219.1, based on safety evaluations conducted within 28 days following infusion. Phase II: To evaluate the overall response rate (ORR) as measured at day 28 by local assessment. Primary endpoint • Phase I: Dose-Limiting Toxicity (DLT): The primary endpoint for Phase 1 is the evaluation of DLT of MB-CART2219.1 within 28 days after infusion. • Phase II: ORR, defined as the sum of complete remission (CR) and complete remission with incomplete hematologic recovery (CRi) at Day 28, as assessed locally.
DualCALM-01.Secondary objectives and endpoints: Secondary objectives: To evaluate - The safety of MB-CART2219.1; - To evaluate treatment response, duration of response and relapse after treatment with MB-CART2219.1; - To assess phenotype, expansion and persistence of MB-CART2219.1; - To correlate treatment response to CD19 and CD22 expression on leukemic blast cells at baseline; - To evaluate the resources consumed for this strategy during the whole conduction of the study (2 years). Secondary endpoint: Safety Profile: • Number and detailed description of adverse events (AEs) reported during the 2 years following infusion, graded according to CTCAE v5.0. Response to CAR-T cells: • Overall Response Rate (ORR) at Month 3 post-infusion. • Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) Response at Day 28 and Month 3 post-infusion, using flow cytometry or qPCR. Survival Outcomes: • DFS: Time from the first complete remission to disease recurrence or progression. • OS: Time from infusion to death from any cause. • DoR: Time from the initial response to disease recurrence or progression, measured up to 2 years post-infusion. Biological Outcomes: • Peripheral Blood Monitoring: Quantification of MB-CART2219.1 levels and normal B-cell counts throughout the 2-year follow-up period. • CD19 and CD22 Expression: Measurement of CD19 and CD22 expression levels at baseline and at the time of relapse, if applicable.
DualCALM-01.Design of the study: This phase I/IIA is a single arm, prospective, open-label study that combines (i) the continual reassessment method (CRM) dose-finding phase I design for evaluation of safety, and (ii) a single-stage phase II design for efficacy evaluation. Phase 1 dose evaluation/escalation part to define the recommended phase II dose of MB-CART2219.1 in patients aged ≥ 18 years. Dose escalation will be based on cohorts of 3 patients treated at the same dose level. The first cohort will be administered at Dose Level 1. Then, based on Bayesian actualization of DLT probabilities, each subsequent cohort will be treated at the estimated MTD over 4 dose levels, unless dose skipping. In case of DLT at Dose Level 1, the fallback dose of Dose Level 0 will be tested. Phase 2 to assess the objective clinical response with MB-CART2219.1 at day 28. After the MTD has been defined (phase I), the patients treated at this dose level will be assessed for efficacy
DualCALM-01.Population of study participants: Adults with R/R B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (BCP-ALL)
DualCALM-01.Inclusion criteria: 1. Age ≥ 18 years and < 70 years at inclusion 2. Relapsed or refractory BCP-cell ALL with ≥ 5 % bone marrow blasts meeting either of the following criteria: a. Second or greater relapse b. Any relapse after allogeneic SCT must be ≥ 3 months from SCT to the time of apheresis c. Refractory at relapse (not achieving a CR after one cycle of chemotherapy for relapsed leukemia) Patients must have exhausted relevant authorised, on-label and accessible treatment options 3. Ph+ ALL must be intolerant or failed two lines of TKI therapy. 4. CD19 or CD22 expression demonstrated in BM or peripheral blood by flow cytometry within 3 weeks prior study inclusion. 5. ECOG performance score of 0-2 6. Absolute CD3+ T cell count ≥100/µl 7. No childbearing potential or negative pregnancy test at screening and before chemotherapy in women with childbearing potential 8. Signed and dated informed consent/assent by patients before to start any trial-specific procedure
DualCALM-01.Exclusion criteria: 1. CNS Involvement: Disease involvement of the central nervous system at the time of MB-CART2219.1 lymphodepletion. 2. Recent Medication: One of the following previous medications • Systemic chemotherapies, corticosteroids (with the exception of physiologic replacement dosing), tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI), intrathecal therapy within 7 days prior to leukapheresis • Fludarabine/clofarabine or immunosuppressive drugs (e.g., calcineurin inhibitors) and antibodies or antibody-targeted agents (e.g., rituximab, daratumomab, isatuximab, blinatumomab, inotuzumab-ozogamicin) or donor lymphocyte transfusions or radiation therapy within 30 days prior to leukapheresis • Live vaccines within 30 days prior to leukapheresis • Alemtuzumab within 3 months prior to leukapheresis, 3. Administration of other investigational product between apheresis and MB-CART2219.1 infusion, 4. Active clinically significant CNS disease (including but not limited to uncontrolled seizure disorders, cerebrovascular ischemia or haemorrhage, dementia, paralysis), 5. Active GVHD or immunosuppression requirement (hydrocortisone > 12 mg/sqm/day or equivalent), 6. Organ failure, defined as a cardiac ejection fraction < 45%; calculated glomerular filtrate rate < 30 mL / min; or bilirubin> 3 times the upper limit of normal, 7. History of uncontrolled cancer for the last 2 years, with the exception of basal cell carcinoma or carcinoma in situ of the cervix, 8. Viral infection: Known positive serology for HIV-1 and -2, HTLV-1 and -2, or active hepatitis B or C infection. 9. Positive SARS-Cov2 by PCR on nasal swab, 10. Personal history of autoimmune disease, 11. Contraindication of investigational medicinal product, of auxiliary medicinal products and of trial related procedures 12. Female patients of child-bearing potential not willing to practice a highly effective form of birth control from leukapheresis up to 12 months after MB-CART2219.1 infusion, 13. Male patients of fathering potential not willing to practice a highly effective form of birth control from leukapheresis and up to 12 months after MB-CART2219.1 infusion, 14. Concurrent participation in another interventional trial that could interact with this trial, e.g., CAR T trials.
DualCALM-01.Investigational medicinal product: Autologous T cells ex vivo lentivirally transduced with the tandem (anti-) CD19CD22 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) construct and expanded (MB- CART2219.1) in a 7 days manufacturing process. In cases where the lymphodepletion regimen cannot be initiated as scheduled, the product may be cryopreserved for later use. Dose escalation: • Dose Level 0: 0.25 x 10^6 CAR-T cells/kg = fallback dose • Dose Level 1: 0.5 x 10^6 CAR-T cells/kg • Dose Level 2: 1.0 x 10^6 CAR-T cells/kg • Dose Level 3: 2.0 x 10^6 CAR-T cells/kg The first cohort will be administered at Dose Level 1. Then, based on Bayesian actualization of DLT probabilities, each subsequent cohort will be treated at the estimated MTD over 4 dose levels, unless dose skipping. In case of DLT at Dose Level 1, the fallback dose of Dose Level 0 will be tested. Marketing authorization: no
DualCALM-01.Interventions added for the study: • Leukapheresis to collect T-cells • Before CAR19/22-T infusion, lymphodepletion course composed of cyclophosphamide (500 mg/sqm/d, D-3 to D-2) and fludarabine (40 mg/sqm/d, D-4 to D-2).
DualCALM-01.Expected benefits for the participants a: Academic production of a new CAR-T cells responding at an actual unmet medical need. While the CAR19/22-T targets two different antigens, it is expected to decrease the risk of relapse that would occur through down regulation of both CD19 and CD22 antigens.
DualCALM-01.Risks and burdens added by the study: Evaluation of the safety of MB-CART2219.1 a new autologous CAR-T cells. Due to the very advance stages of the diseases considered for inclusion in the trial, the potential benefit of MB-CART2219.1 therapy outweighs the potential risks of the therapy in our study population. Other risks are related to auxiliary medicinal products and to interventions added by the study
DualCALM-01.Number of centres: - 5 clinical sites (Paris Saint-Louis, Lyon, Bordeaux, Marseille, Nantes) - 1 ATMP platform (MEARY, Saint-Louis, APHP, Paris)
DualCALM-01.Duration of the study: Inclusion period: 18 months Participation period (treatment + follow-up): 2 years Total duration: 3.5 years
DualCALM-01.Number of enrolments expected per site a: It is expected that 4 patients will be included by site (0.22 patient/site/month)
DualCALM-01.Statistical analysis: Safety/Efficacy analyses Analysis will be based on the main analysis set, i.e., all patients who are treated with MB-CART2219.1. Phase 1 data will be recorded sequentially according to the CRM A working parametric model is first assumed, based on the expected DLT rate at each dose level, assuming a monotonic relationship, with parameter estimation based on recorded data with a noninformative prior. It allows borrowing of information across dose levels along the trial. Before inclusion, model characteristics will be evaluated using a pre-trial simulation study. Analysis will use the dfcrm R package (Cheung YK. Dose finding by the continual reassessment method. Chapman& Hall/CRC Biostatistics Series: Taylor and Francis; 2011). Phase 2 data will be analysed in intent-to-treat, based 95% confidence interval of the all the endpoints. Calculation hypotheses for the number of participants required and the result. A one-stage Bayesian continual reassessment method (CRM) will be used with cohort size of 3. A maximum sample size of 18 ensures a probability of correct select of 0.5 for the CRM, assuming a 1.8 odds ratio for the true logistic dose-toxicity curve and using a basic arbitrary skeleton with DL2 as the anticipated MTD1. Method for taking into account missing Missing data on outcome will not be imputed except for primary outcome of phase 2 data considered as failure if missing.
DualCALM-01.Study will have a Data Safety Monitoring: An independent 3-member data safety monitoring board (DSMB) will be designed and operate according to a separate charter. It will review the trial and decide whether to stop the protocol according to safety events.
